chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

A woman came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'Marry me off.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Who is for this one?' A man stood up and said, 'I am, O Messenger of Allah, marry me to her.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'What will you give her?' He said, 'I have nothing.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'No.' She repeated, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) repeated the question, but no one stood up except that man. Then she repeated again. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said on the third time: 'Do you know anything from the Quran?' He said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'I have married you to her on whatever you know from the Quran, so teach her it.'

key_terms.فَعَلِّمْهَا إِيَّاهُ: So teach her it (instruction to impart knowledge)
key_terms.مَا تُعْطِيهَا: What will you give her? (referring to dowry)
key_terms.مَنْ لِهَذِهِ: Who is for this one? (offer of marriage)
key_terms.مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ: From the Quran (referring to memorized verses)

ai.seo_question: What can serve as a dowry (mahr) if a man has no wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith, found in *Al-Kafi*, establishes the principle that spiritual knowledge can substitute for material wealth in the dowry (*mahr*), reflecting the Shia emphasis on the intrinsic value of Quranic literacy. The Prophet’s instruction for the husband to teach her underscores the mutual educational responsibility within the marital bond, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the rights and duties of spouses.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A woman came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so she said, ‘Get me married’. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Who is for this one?’ So a man stood up and he said, ‘I will marry her, O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>!’ So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘What will you give her?’ So he said, ‘There is nothing for me’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘No’. 
He<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘So she re-iterated, and Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> repeated the speech. But, no one stood up apart from that man. Then she re-iterated. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said during the third time: ‘Are you good with anything from the Quran?’ He said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘I<sup>saww</sup> hereby marry the two of you upon a (dower of) whatever you are good at from the Quran, so you will teach her it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that once a woman came to the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and said, ‘You must give me in marriage.’

The Messenger of Allah, asked, ‘Is there anyone for her?’ A man stood up and said, ‘I am for her, O Messenger of Allah, give her in marriage to me.’ He (the Messenger of Allah) asked, ‘What do you want to give her?’ He replied, ‘I do not have anything.’ He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘No, I will not give her in marriage to you.’ She repeated and the Messenger of Allah also repeated his question to people, but no one other than that man said anything. She repeated again and on the third time the Messenger of Allah asked that man, ‘Do you know something from the Quran well?’ He replied, ‘Yes, I know from the Quran.’ He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘I give her in marriage to you to teach her what you know well of the Quran.’”
